vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: skywork-music-maker
Version: 1.0.1

The skywork-music-maker skill is a legitimate integration for the Mureka AI music generation platform. The Python script `scripts/mureka.py` provides a clean CLI for interacting with the official API (https://api.mureka.ai) to generate songs, lyrics, and handle audio uploads. The documentation in `SKILL.md` and `README.md` is well-structured, providing clear instructions for the AI agent to convert natural language into structured music prompts without any evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized execution.

llm.summary: The skill appears to do what it claims (uses the Mureka API to generate music), but there is an internal inconsistency in the metadata vs. runtime instructions and some operational behaviors you should be aware of before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description and the code/instructions align: the skill calls the Mureka API to generate songs, instrumentals, uploads reference/vocal files, and saves generated audio locally. However, registry metadata at the top claims no required environment variables while SKILL.md and the included CLI script require a MUREKA_API_KEY — this mismatch is incoherent and could lead to the agent or platform not prompting for the API key correctly.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to convert freeform text into structured prompts, present them to the user for confirmation, and then call api.mureka.ai. It explicitly sends lyrics, prompts, and uploaded audio to Mureka and saves outputs locally. The instructions do not ask the agent to read unrelated local secrets or system files. Important operational behavior: uploads of reference tracks or vocal samples are performed to the remote API when requested — users should expect their audio to leave the machine.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only skill) so no external archives are downloaded during install. A small Python CLI (scripts/mureka.py) is included; it uses requests and performs network calls to the declared API. No obfuscated download URLs or third-party install sources are present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill legitimately requires a single API credential (MUREKA_API_KEY) and network access — that is proportionate to its stated purpose. The concern is the inconsistency: registry metadata lists no required env vars while SKILL.md marks MUREKA_API_KEY as required and the script enforces it. This inconsistency could hide the need to provide a key or cause a runtime failure. No other unrelated secrets or credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request permanent/always-on inclusion and does not modify other skills or system-wide settings. Autonomous invocation (agent can call the skill) is allowed but that is the platform default; nothing else amplifies this privilege.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a straightforward Mureka API client for music generation, but before installing: 1) Verify you are comfortable sending any reference audio or vocal samples to https://api.mureka.ai (uploads are performed when you request vocal cloning or style-transfer). 2) Provide a MUREKA_API_KEY environment variable — SKILL.md and the script require it, despite registry metadata saying none; the mismatch is likely a packaging error. 3) Review scripts/mureka.py yourself (it is small and readable) and run the skill in a controlled environment first (or sandbox) if you are cautious. 4) Be aware of legal/privacy issues around vocal cloning and copyrighted reference tracks. 5) If you don’t already have a Mureka account, create one and confirm billing details; the skill will bill usage to that account. If anything about the source/origin of this skill is unknown or you cannot confirm the publisher, consider running it in isolation or declining installation until provenance is clarified.
